proposals: The Finance Ministry should add to the Budget’s statement of revenue foregone an annual estimate of central excise not collected on petrol displaced by ethanol, so that a cost this piece models at about ₹21,500 crore at E20 is reported by the government itself as blending rises.

The GST Council should publish the revenue analysis behind any dedicated state levy on ethanol, including the rate needed for VAT parity, so that states can see that a 5% SGST recovers only a fraction of what full parity at roughly 27% would.

PPAC should publish each year the petrol volume displaced by ethanol alongside petrol export volumes and realisations, so that the claim that freed petrol is exported — about 8 MMT at E20 — can be checked against official data rather than inferred.

The Department of Food and Public Distribution should publish installed and actually utilised ethanol distillation capacity, by feedstock, every ethanol supply year, so that the binding constraint the piece identifies — feedstock and utilisation, not nameplate capacity — is tracked in public.
